policies.name: Emergency Order Halting Short Selling in Financial Stocks
policies.intendedEffect: To restore fair and orderly securities markets and stabilize prices - curb the rapid downward trend of prices during this financial crisis.
policies.actualImpact: Severe degradation in market quality - bid ask spreads widened dramatically, volatility increased

policies.name: Term Asset-Backed Securities Loan Facility
policies.intendedEffect: Intended to increase demand for asset-backed securities (ABS) and encourage more lending to households and small businesses.
policies.actualImpact: Played a critical role in preventing the shutdown of lending to consumers and small businesses. Implying that the returns for small businesses should have stopped plunging.

policies.name: commercial paper funding facility
policies.intendedEffect: Intended to ensure firms have enough liquidity to meet their operational needs so they don't go bankrupt.
policies.actualImpact: Firms that were eligible for the CPFF were able to mitigate financing disruptions and led to an increase in profitability and short-term earnings forecasts. Spillover effects also led to increase in general public liquidity.

policies.name: term auction facility
policies.intendedEffect: Provide emergency liquidity and reduce the liquidity risk premium in the interbank market, and hence bring down the significantly elevated London interbank offered rate (Libor).
policies.actualImpact: Literature documented mixed results, but seem to imply that the policy effectively relieved the liquidity strains and brought down the Libor.

policies.name: decimalization
policies.actualImpact: bid-ask spreads fell dramatically. increased liquidity from decimalization increased firm performance - slightly higher returns
